# ButtonGroup accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

<!-- intro:start -->

A ButtonGroup puts several Buttons in one set. This report rates only what the group adds: the group role and name, the layout, the dividers, and the focus order. Each button inherits the [Button report](../Button/accessibility.md).

<!-- intro:end -->

| Result                   | Count |
| :----------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports              | 9     |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports    | 1     |
| ❌ Does Not Support      | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable        | 28    |
| ↗ Inherited (see Button) | 17    |
| 🚩 Flagged               | 3/10  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.** <!-- 1.4.11:gap:start -->The buttons keep the Button focus ripple as their default focus indicator. Its contrast can fall below `3:1`. `disableRipple` or `disableFocusRipple` on the group removes it from each button.<!-- 1.4.11:gap:end -->
- Inherits ⚠️ **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)** from [Button](../Button/accessibility.md).
- Inherits ⚠️ **4.1.3 Status Messages** from [Button](../Button/accessibility.md).

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- The group shows its buttons in DOM order, in a row or in a column. It does not reverse the order.
- The order of the children is an author decision.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through a horizontal group.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through a vertical group.
3. Compare the focus order with the visual order in each group.
4. Read each group with the screen-reader virtual cursor.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->focus and the reading order move in the reading direction in a horizontal group, and from top to bottom in a vertical group.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- The dividers between the buttons have these contrasts against the adjacent colors, in light mode:
  - `outlined` and `text`: the `main` color at `50%` on a white page, `1.76:1` (`warning`) to `2.39:1` (`secondary`). With `color="inherit"`, `1.74:1`.
  - `contained`: the `dark` color between two `main` fills, `1.13:1` (`error`) to `1.92:1` (`info`). With `color="inherit"`, `grey[400]` on `grey[300]` is `1.42:1`.
- In an `outlined` group, the divider is the border of the next button. So the `outlined` border has the same contrast.
- WCAG does not require a boundary when text or an icon identifies the control (Understanding 1.4.11). Each button has its own label, so the dividers do not need `3:1`.
- The focus indicator is the Button focus ripple. `disableRipple` and `disableFocusRipple` on the group pass to each button, so one group prop can remove the indicator from all buttons. `disableElevation` removes the focus shadow of a `contained` button.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the dividers of each variant in use against the colors next to them.
2. Measure the `outlined` border against the page.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a button in the group.
4. Measure the focus indicator against the colors next to it.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->each button can be identified by its label, and the focus indicator is at least `3:1`.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The group name, from `aria-label`, describes the purpose of the set of buttons. Each button keeps its own label.
- Whether the group name is useful is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the `aria-label` of each ButtonGroup.
2. Read each name without the buttons.

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->each group name tells the purpose of the set, for example "Text alignment", not "Basic button group".<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `ButtonGroup.test.js`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- The root has `role="group"`, so assistive technology reports the buttons as one set. A unit test confirms that the buttons are inside the group element. An author can replace it with the `role` prop.
- The author names the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The component does not warn when the name is missing. A group without a name still conveys the grouping.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into a ButtonGroup that has an `aria-label`.
3. Listen to the announcement.
4. Do the test again with a group that has no `aria-label`.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the screen reader announces the group role and name, and the name and role of the button. A group with no name is announced as a group.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.7 Focus Visible · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `ButtonGroup.test.js` · Playwright

<!-- 2.4.7:start -->

- Keyboard focus shows the Button focus ripple, inside the button, so the neighbors cannot cover it. A Playwright test confirms that keyboard focus changes how the button looks.
- In a `contained` group without the theme ring, the focused button also gets a shadow. The next button can cover the edge of this shadow.
- With `focusVisible: true` on the theme, the focused button gets the outline ring and `z-index: 1`. The neighbors touch the focused button. In an `outlined` group, they overlap it by 1 px. The ring paints above them. A unit test in a real browser confirms the `z-index`. In a `contained` group, the ring replaces the shadow.
- `disableRipple` or `disableFocusRipple` on the group removes the ripple from each button.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through the buttons of a horizontal and a vertical group.
2. Make sure that the focus indicator of each button is fully visible.
3. Set `focusVisible: true` on the theme and do the test again.

<!-- 2.4.7:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.7:pass:start -->the focus indicator of each button is fully visible, and the adjacent buttons do not cover the ring.<!-- 2.4.7:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `ButtonGroup.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `button-name` ✅, `duplicate-id-aria` ✅, `link-name` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- The group has `role="group"` and the name from `aria-label`. `disabled` on the group disables each button that does not set its own `disabled` prop. A button with `disabled={false}` stays enabled. Unit tests confirm this. The axe-core ARIA rules pass on the demos.
- The group does not keep a pressed or selected state. For a set of toggles, the author sets `aria-pressed` on each button, as in the `ButtonGroupA11ySemanticStates` fixture, or uses ToggleButtonGroup. axe-core checks these attributes on the fixture.
- In a split button, the author sets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-label` on the arrow button. The SplitButton demo and the `ButtonGroupA11ySemanticStates` fixture show this pattern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the arrow button of the SplitButton demo.
3. Listen to the announcement.
4. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to open the menu.
5. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> to move focus back to the arrow button.
6. Listen to the announcement again.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->the arrow button announces its name, that it opens a menu, and "collapsed" or "expanded".<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.4 Resize Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.4:start -->

- The buttons scale with the text size, and the group grows with them. A Playwright test confirms that the variant demo does not clip or overflow at a 200% text size.

<!-- 1.4.4:end -->

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- A horizontal group is an `inline-flex` row that does not wrap. When the group is too wide, each button wraps its label first. When that is not enough, the group overflows its container, and the page scrolls horizontally.
- A Playwright test confirms that the three-button variant demo does not scroll at 320 px. A screenshot records the `ButtonGroupA11yWideGroup` fixture, with five buttons, at 320 px. The test viewer hides horizontal overflow, so the screenshot shows the group clipped at the right edge.
- The number of buttons is an author decision. To fix a wide group, set `orientation="vertical"` on small screens, for example with `useMediaQuery`.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

#### 1.4.12 Text Spacing · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.12:start -->

- The buttons wrap their labels, and the group grows with them. A Playwright test confirms this with the WCAG text-spacing values.

<!-- 1.4.12:end -->

#### 2.4.3 Focus Order · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `ButtonGroup.test.js`

<!-- 2.4.3:start -->

- Each button is a tab stop in DOM order. `orientation` changes only the layout, so the order is the same in both orientations. A disabled group removes its buttons from the tab order. Unit tests confirm this. For the manual check, see 1.3.2.

<!-- 2.4.3:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** No auto-starting moving, blinking, or auto-updating content.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.4.13 Focus Appearance.** The buttons keep the Button focus ripple, which does not meet it. `🚩`
- **2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), 44 px.** The buttons keep the Button sizes, which are less than 44 px high. `🚩`

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The ButtonGroup wrapper, rendered through its documented API. The buttons inside it inherit the [Button report](../Button/accessibility.md).
- **Automated.** axe-core in the Playwright test harness, on the ButtonGroup demos and fixtures in [`button-group.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/button-group/button-group.a11y.json). Interaction tests are in `ButtonGroup.test.js`.
- **Assistive-technology review.** Not done yet. The flagged criteria come from a review of the source. A review with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver must still confirm them.

<!-- scope:end -->
